core_obligations: Quote that a section of a smooth morphism is a regular immersion, and reduce the operator identity to s^! cap p^*[Z] = [Z] for an integral closed subscheme Z of X, which suffices because the assumptions are preserved by base change (proof lines 13445-13450).
Shrink P to an open neighbourhood of s(Z) so that p has fixed relative dimension r, and compute p^*[Z] = [p^{-1}(Z)]_{n+r} for dim_delta(Z) = n (proof lines 13451-13453).

Observe that s(X) cap p^{-1}(Z) = s(Z) scheme theoretically and that it is a closed subscheme regularly embedded of codimension r, then conclude by the fundamental-class lemma (proof lines 13454-13457).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to one cycle class and shrink to fixed relative dimension (proof lines 13445-13453).
Identify the scheme theoretic intersection with s(Z) (proof lines 13454-13456).
Conclude with the fundamental-class lemma (proof lines 13456-13457).
difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism p : P -> X of schemes locally of finite type over the base situation and a section s : X -> P, the lemma asserts two things: that s is a regular immersion, and that 1 = s^! o p^* in A^*(X), where p^* is the flat pullback bivariant class (statement lines 13434-13442). The first assertion is quoted, but the operator identity is proved by reducing to a single cycle class: since the assumptions are preserved by base change it suffices to show s^! cap p^*[Z] = [Z] for an integral closed subscheme Z of X (proof lines 13447-13450). After shrinking P to a neighbourhood of s(Z) one may assume p has fixed relative dimension r, so every component of p^{-1}(Z) has dimension n + r and p^*[Z] = [p^{-1}(Z)]_{n+r}; the key observation is that s(X) cap p^{-1}(Z) = s(Z) scheme theoretically and that this is a regularly embedded closed subscheme of codimension r, so the fundamental-class lemma for a regularly embedded divisor applies (proof lines 13451-13457). Recognising that the scheme theoretic intersection computes s^! on the class is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
